Drivers¶

These are typically pieces of test equipment that are used to measure, stimulate or otherwise “test” the device under test (DUT). Examples of test equipment could be power supplies, oscilloscopes, JTAG programmers, etc..

Drivers required for a particular DUT are listed in the config section of scripts. For example:

"config": {
  // fail_fast: if true (default), testing will stop on first failed test
  "fail_fast": false,
  // list of driver code to initialize the test environment, must be specified
  // Drivers may or may not have args
  "drivers": ["public.prism.drivers.fake.hwdrv_fake",
              ["public.prism.drivers.fake.hwdrv_fakeArgs", {"k0": 0, "k1": 1}] ]
},

Prism will load/init each driver that is listed, when the script is validated. A driver listed with arguments (a list of the driver path and a dict, like hwdrv_fakeArgs above) has the dict passed to discover_channels(args).

The python file specified MUST have a class called HWDriver. See the fake example for implementation details and documentation.

By convention, the driver filename has the prefix hwdrv_<name>.py.

The Drivers files are stored by convention in a separate path relative to scripts in order to isolate them. Drivers are typically common to test multiple products.

Discover Channels¶

The important method of the HWDriver class is discover_channels.

discover_channels method returns a list of dictionaries that represent the connected hardware used in the test system. Every driver that reports a number of channels must report the same number, otherwise the script fails validation. A driver that reports 0 channels is a shared resource for all channels, see Shared Drivers. The list may contain one item that is shared among all the attached test jigs, or it might be one item per test jig.

If there are multiple hardware items, the list of those items must be in the same order across the different hardware types. For example, if each test jig has a Teensy4 and a Segger programmer, the list of Teensy4s and Seggers must be in the same order. In this example, both Segger and the Teensy4s are connected via USB, and if a prescribed USB (cabling) setup is used (one hub per test jig) then the USB path can be used to synchronize the two lists. This is done in the examples provided.

Per the code documentation, discover_channels must return a dictionary with prescribed keys.

def discover_channels(self):
    """ determine the number of channels, and popultae hw drivers into shared state

    [ {"id": i,                    # ~slot number of the channel (see Note 1)
       "version": <VERSION>,       # version of the driver
       "hwdrv": <object>,          # instance of your hardware driver

       # optional
       "close": None,              # register a callback on closing the channel, or None
       "play": jig_closed_detect   # function for detecting jig closed
       "play_poll_sec": 1          # seconds between play calls, 0.2 to 2, default 1
       "show_pass_fail": jig_led   # function for indicating pass/fail (like LED)
       "show_msg": jig_display     # function for indicating test status (like display)

       # not part of the required block
       "unique_id": <unique_id>,   # unique id of the hardware (for tracking purposes)
       ...
      }, ...
    ]

    Note:
    1) The hw driver objects are expected to have an 'slot' field, the lowest
       id is assigned to channel 0, the next highest to channel 1, etc
       A shared driver (returns 0 channels) is not assigned a channel, all channels use it.

    :return: <#>, <driver_type>, <list> (use Zero for a device shared across all channels)
        where
            #:      >0 number of channels,
                    0 does not indicate num channels, like a shared hardware driver
                    <0 error
            driver_type: String constant identifying Installed drivers type
            list:   List of installed driver dicts
    """

Prism calls the play function every second to see if the jig has closed, and starts the test when it does. A driver can set play_poll_sec to change this, from 0.2 to 2 seconds, for example so a test restarts sooner after the jig closes. A value outside the range is logged and set to the nearest limit, and a value that is not a number is logged and the default of 1 second is used.

Shared Drivers¶

A driver that returns 0 channels is shared by all channels, for example one label printer for all the test jigs. Its driver items are not assigned to a channel, and self.shared_state.get_drivers(self.chan, type=…) returns them for every channel, along with that channel’s own drivers. get_drivers(None, type=…) returns only the shared drivers.

  • At least one driver of the script must set the number of channels, a script with only shared drivers fails validation.

  • A shared driver must return at least one item in its list, otherwise validation fails.

  • The play, show_pass_fail, show_msg and jig_reset functions of a shared driver, if set, are called by every channel. A shared driver usually sets them to None.

  • The channels run at the same time, so lock shared equipment while a channel uses it, see Locking Shared Equipment.

A driver can support both, with a script argument. For example, the brother_ql and agilent_dso_usb_1 drivers with {“only_one”: true} expect one instrument shared by all channels, and finding more than one is an error. Without it, there is one instrument per channel, in USB hub port order:

"drivers": ["public.prism.drivers.fake.hwdrv_fake",
            ["public.prism.drivers.brother_ql.hwdrv_brother_ql", {"only_one": true}]]

Equipment is shared by the jigs (channels) of one Prism computer. Sharing one instrument between Prism computers is not supported: Prism does not lock it between computers, and a driver that resets its instrument when a script loads would reset it in the middle of the other computer’s test.

Locking Shared Equipment¶

Each channel runs its test items in its own thread. Without a lock, two channels can send commands to a shared instrument at the same time, and each reads the other’s settings or results.

Hold self.shared_lock(<name>) for the whole sequence of commands that must not be interleaved, for example set up, trigger and measure. Every channel that uses the instrument must use the same name, such as the driver type. Use with so the lock is released when the item fails, times out or is aborted:

with self.shared_lock("AGILENT_DSO_USB_1"):
    self.dso.write(':AUT CHAN{}'.format(self.dso_ch))
    vpp = self.dso.query(':MEASure:VPP? CHANnel{}'.format(self.dso_ch))

Keep the time the lock is held short, the other channels wait for it. A test that holds a shared instrument for a long time makes the jigs take turns.

Slot Number¶

When implementing python code to implement tests, there is a channel (self.chan) number and a slot number. The channel is how Prism indexes the running threads, usually from 0 to a max of 7. The slot number is a number used to setup configuration of the physical system.

Adding Test Equipment¶

Test equipment, like an oscilloscope, a power supply or a programmer, is added to a test jig with a driver. Start from the included driver closest to your equipment, see Included Drivers, and copy its folder into public/prism/drivers with a new name.

  1. One per jig, or shared. Decide if each jig has its own instrument, or one instrument serves all the jigs of the Prism computer. One per jig is simpler and lets the jigs test at the same time. A shared instrument saves cost, but the jigs take turns using it.

  2. Find the instruments. discover_channels finds the instruments on USB, Ethernet or serial. On USB, a driver can find every instrument by its USB vendor and product id. On Ethernet, the instruments are listed in the driver arguments by IP address.

  3. Put them in jig order. With one instrument per jig, channel 0 must get the instrument wired to jig 0, and so on. Order USB instruments by the USB hub port they are plugged into, and use one hub per jig, or the same port on each hub. Order Ethernet instruments by the list of IP addresses. Instruments that report the same number of channels as the jig controller must be in the same order, see Discover Channels.

  4. Fail if one is missing. If an instrument is not found, return an error rather than fewer channels. Skipping a missing instrument moves the next one to the wrong jig.

  5. Wire a shared instrument. A shared instrument with several inputs usually has one input per jig, for example scope input self.chan + 1 for the jig of self.chan. The number of inputs limits the number of jigs.

  6. Lock a shared instrument, see Locking Shared Equipment.

  7. Record it. Return the instrument’s serial number as the unique_id, and record it in a setup item as a string measurement, for a shared instrument also the input used. A problem found later can then be traced to one instrument or input, see Test Equipment.

  8. Test it. Each driver file has a __main__ section to run discover_channels from a terminal, without Prism. Then run the script with prism_dev.py –script <path>, and with Prism. Remember that the discover_channels of some drivers reset their instrument, as the script loads.

  9. Document it. Describe the driver arguments in the discover_channels doc string, and add a README.md to the driver folder with the equipment, how it connects, per jig or shared, and any setup such as udev rules or vendor tools.

The agilent_dso_usb_1 driver and the dso_v0 example do all of the above, for one scope per jig or one shared scope, see agilent_dso_usb_1.

VISA¶

VISA is a test equipment control protocol. See VISA for more information.

Prism includes these two PyPi VISA modules,

  • pyvisa

  • PyVISA-py

An example of VISA driver based hardware is provided in the agilent_dso_usb_1 driver example. It finds the scope on USB by default, or on Ethernet (VXI-11) with driver arguments, see agilent_dso_usb_1.

On USB, Prism in its Docker container needs no udev rule, see Deployment. To run the driver or prism_dev.py on the host, your user account needs access to the scope, either for all USB devices with sudo ./udev-install-usbusers.sh from the scripts repo, or just for the scope with this rule (DSO7000 series, USB id 0957:175d),

echo 'SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTR{idVendor}=="0957", ATTR{idProduct}=="175d", MODE="0666"' | \
    sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-agilent-dso.rules
sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo udevadm trigger

Then unplug and plug in the scope’s USB cable. Without access, pyvisa logs Found a USB INSTR device whose serial number cannot be read and the driver finds no scope.

Note

Error: Found a device whose serial number cannot be read

This error can happen if your user account doesn’t have correct privileges.

See: stackoverflow

Included Drivers¶

These drivers are included in public/prism/drivers. Each driver’s hwdrv_*.py file documents its arguments, and several have a README.md with setup details. The driver type is the type to use with self.shared_state.get_drivers(self.chan, type=…).

The example scripts are in public/prism/scripts/example. segger is a placeholder, not complete, and common holds shared helpers, it is not a driver.

Note

The vendor programming tools used by nrfprog (Nordic nrfjprog) and stlinkv3mods (ST STM32CubeProgrammer) are not included in the scripts. Each Prism station installs them in the tools folder of its public folder (the folder prism.sh is run from), for example ~/prism/public/tools/ on a station set up as in Deployment. This folder is ignored by git, is not synced from Lente, and Prism sees it through its existing public mount. Each driver’s README.md has the install steps, and the driver checks its tool runs when Prism loads a script.

  • stlinkv3mods - see public/prism/drivers/stlinkv3mods/README.md

  • nrfprog - see public/prism/drivers/nrfprog/README.md

Segger J-Link is installed in the Prism Docker image (/opt/SEGGER/JLink) and needs no host install.

fake¶

Simulated hardware, so the example scripts run without a jig. hwdrv_fake makes NUM_CHANNELS channels (1 to 8, set in the file), and its show_pass_fail and show_msg functions only log. hwdrv_fakeArgs shows how a driver takes arguments, the second item of the driver in the script, which can be any JSON value.

  • Driver types: FAKE, FakeWithArgs

  • Start here to learn the driver API, hwdrv_fake.py documents every field of discover_channels.

  • Because a shared driver cannot set the number of channels, several examples use fake to set it next to a shared driver.

agilent_dso_usb_1¶

Agilent InfiniiVision oscilloscope, tested with a DSO7104B, using VISA on USB or Ethernet. discover_channels resets each scope it finds (*RST), so loading the script resets the scope. Only the models in the driver’s WHITE_LIST are used.

  • Driver type: AGILENT_DSO_USB_1, the scope’s serial number is the unique_id

  • {“only_one”: true} - one scope shared by all channels, finding more than one is an error. Without it, there is one scope per channel.

  • {“interface”: “ethernet”, “ip”: …} - scopes on Ethernet (VXI-11), USB is the default. ip is one IP address, or a list with one IP per channel, in channel order. Every scope in the list must be found.

  • On USB, the scopes are ordered by the USB hub port they are plugged into.

"drivers": [
  "public.prism.drivers.fake.hwdrv_fake",
  ["public.prism.drivers.agilent_dso_usb_1.hwdrv_agilent_dso_usb_1", {"only_one": true}]
]

"drivers": [
  ["public.prism.drivers.agilent_dso_usb_1.hwdrv_agilent_dso_usb_1",
   {"interface": "ethernet", "ip": ["192.168.1.100", "192.168.1.101"]}]
]

The first is one shared scope on USB, the second one scope per jig on Ethernet, with two jigs. The dso_v0 example test code works with both. A shared scope uses input self.chan + 1 for each jig, so up to 4 jigs on a 4 input scope, and is locked while a channel uses it. A scope per jig uses input 1. See VISA for USB access on the host.

brother_ql¶

Brother QL label printer (QL-700) on USB, to print a label such as a serial number barcode.

  • Driver type: Brother_QL

  • {“only_one”: true} - one printer shared by all channels. Without it, there is one printer per channel, in USB hub port order.

  • {“test_label”: true} - print a test label when the script loads, the script fails validation if it cannot print.

ble_listener¶

Listens for Bluetooth LE advertisements, for example to check a DUT advertises, using the station’s Bluetooth adapter. It is always shared, so another driver sets the number of channels.

  • Driver type: BLE_LISTENER

  • Prism uses the host BlueZ through the D-Bus mount in prism.sh.

  • Loading a script fails if the Bluetooth adapter is off or missing. Test the host with python3 blelistener_cli.py scan -t 30 from the driver folder.

scanners¶

USB barcode scanner in keyboard mode (Datalogic). It makes one channel, and its play function restarts the script for each scan, see Barcode Count Example.

  • Driver type: SCANNER

  • A scanner in keyboard mode types into the window that has focus, so scans cannot be told apart by scanner. More scanners still make one channel.

teensy4¶

Teensy 4 based jig controller, the reference Interface Controller. The Teensy4 runs the Prism simpleRPC server firmware, from teensy4/server, which gives Python access to its pins.

  • Driver types: TEENSY4, and TEENSY4_PROG for hwdrv_teensy4_prog

  • hwdrv_teensy4 makes one channel per Teensy4, in USB path order. The jig closed GPIO, if set, is its play function, and it has show_pass_fail and jig_reset functions.

  • hwdrv_teensy4_prog programs the firmware into a new Teensy4, with one Teensy4 connected, teensy4_ProgFresh_0.scr. teensy4_Update_0.scr updates the firmware.

  • The firmware version is checked, a Teensy4 running another version is not used.

  • Building the firmware, see public/prism/drivers/teensy4/server/README.md

A4401_BOND¶

Sistemi BOND (Bed of Nails Design), a Teensy 4.1 based tester with configurable analog and digital pins, a DUT supply and a battery emulator, see BOND.

  • Driver types: A4401_BOND, and A4401_BOND_PROG for hwdrv_A4401_BOND_prog

  • hwdrv_A4401_BOND takes the path of the Pogo board header definition file, and makes one channel per BOND, in USB path order.

  • hwdrv_A4401_BOND_prog programs the firmware into a new BOND, bond_progfresh_0.scr.

  • Setup and pin rules, see public/prism/drivers/A4401_BOND/README.md

nrfprog¶

Programs Nordic nRF devices with nrfjprog, through a SEGGER J-Link probe, such as the one on a Nordic nRF DK.

  • Driver type: NRFJPROG, the probe serial number is the unique_id

  • One channel per probe, in USB path order. The serial number selects the probe for nrfjprog.

  • The nRF Command Line Tools are installed on each station, see the note above and public/prism/drivers/nrfprog/README.md.

stlinkv3mods¶

Programs STM32 devices with STM32CubeProgrammer, through an ST-LINK/V3 probe, such as the STLINK-V3MODS.

  • Driver type: STLINKV3MODS, the probe serial number is the unique_id

  • One channel per probe, in USB path order. A probe that fails the version check is skipped.

  • STM32CubeProgrammer is installed on each station, see the note above and public/prism/drivers/stlinkv3mods/README.md.

prism_play¶

Starts a test from the command line instead of a jig, for example from a GitHub Actions runner to test firmware in CI. There is no hardware, a named pipe per channel takes the play command.

  • Driver type: PrismPlay

  • {“work_dir”: <path>, “channels”: <#>} - work_dir is required, the folder under public for the pipes. channels defaults to 1.

  • Run prism_play_cli.py to start a channel, see public/prism/drivers/prism_play/README.md and README_github_prism_ci.md.
